title: How to plan a holiday when everyone wants something different
author: Matt
intro: One wants a beach, one wants a city and one wants mountains. You don't always have to pick one. Here's how to plan a holiday that gives everyone something they wanted.
seo_title: When everyone wants a different holiday: how to plan one trip

sections.heading: You might not have to choose
sections.text: Beach or city? Lazy or active? Hot or cool? It often feels as if one person has to give up their idea for someone else's. But plenty of places and plans can give everyone a bit of what they want. Before you hold a vote, see whether you can combine the ideas instead.

sections.heading: Find out what each person actually wants
sections.text: "I want a beach" might really mean "I want to swim every day" or "I want to do nothing for a week". "I want a city" might mean good food, museums or just somewhere lively in the evening. Ask everyone what they'd do on their perfect day. The answers usually overlap more than the place names do, and they're much easier to combine.

sections.heading: Pick somewhere that does both
sections.text:
Some places are made for groups who can't agree. A city with a beach, or a beach with a great old town, keeps the sun-seekers and the sightseers happy in one trip:
- [Barcelona](/destinations/barcelona), [Valencia](/destinations/valencia) and [Lisbon](/destinations/lisbon): big cities with beaches a short trip away
- [Crete](/destinations/crete) and [Madeira](/destinations/madeira): beaches and pools, plus gorges, hikes and towns to explore
- [Lake Garda](/destinations/lake-garda): swimming, boat trips and mountains, with Verona close by
- [Cape Town](/destinations/cape-town), [Sydney](/destinations/sydney) and [San Diego](/destinations/san-diego): further away, but city, beach and wildlife in one

Our [beach holidays](/destinations/beach-holidays) and [city breaks](/destinations/city-breaks) pages are a good place to spot others that appear on both lists.

sections.heading: Split the trip in two
sections.text: A two-centre holiday gives you two different places in one trip: a few days in a city, then a week by the sea, or a mountain cabin followed by a lake. It works best when the two places are connected by a short train or drive, so you don't lose a day travelling in the middle. Lisbon and the [Alentejo](/destinations/alentejo) coast, Verona and [Lake Garda](/destinations/lake-garda), or [Matera](/destinations/matera) and the Puglia coast are easy pairings. Further afield, Tulum's beaches and the calm [Bacalar](/destinations/bacalar) lagoon go well together.

sections.heading: Split the days instead
sections.text:
If you're staying in one place, plan the week so everyone gets their days. Alternate a busy day with a lazy one, or let each person choose one day out. Mornings for sightseeing and afternoons by the pool works well in hot places, when the middle of the day is too hot for walking anyway.

It also helps to agree that people don't have to do everything together. One parent takes the children to the water park while the other goes to the museum, and you meet up for dinner.

sections.heading: Take turns across the year
sections.text: If the ideas really can't be combined, let one person's idea win this time and agree whose turn it is next. A short break later in the year for the runner-up idea can soften the blow. Keep all the ideas that didn't win on a list, so they don't get forgotten.

sections.heading: If you still can't agree, let a draw decide
sections.text: When there's no way to combine everyone's wishes, you need a fair way to choose one. Give everyone the same number of points to spread across the ideas in secret, plus one veto, and let a draw weighted by the points pick the winner. Nobody has to argue, and everyone had the same say. Our post on [fair ways to pick a holiday](/blog/fair-ways-to-pick-a-holiday) explains why it works.

faqs.question: How do you plan a holiday that suits everyone?
faqs.answer: Ask what each person wants from their perfect day, then look for somewhere that does several things at once, like a city with a beach, or split the trip between two places. If that's not possible, use points and a fair draw to choose.

faqs.question: Where is good for a holiday with a beach and a city?
faqs.answer: Barcelona, Valencia and Lisbon in Europe, and Cape Town, Sydney and San Diego further away, all have city life and beaches close together.

faqs.question: What is a two-centre holiday?
faqs.answer: A holiday split between two places, such as a few days in a city and then a week on the coast. It's a good way to give a group two very different kinds of holiday in one trip.
